key_insight: Replacing per-head keys and values with a shared low-rank latent KV cache (Multi-Head Latent Attention, MLA) preserves autoregressive video diffusion quality while drastically reducing the dominant memory and latency cost of per-head KV storage for minute-scale rollouts.
problem_solved: Streaming/long-rollout causal video diffusion is bottlenecked by large per-head KV caches that drive memory usage and latency as generation extends to minutes; the paper addresses reducing that footprint without harming generation fidelity.
method: Introduce Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA): a shared low-rank latent KV cache that replaces separate per-head keys and values with a compact common basis.
Factorize attention state into a small latent dictionary plus lightweight head-specific projections so heads reuse a shared representation while retaining expressivity.
Integrate MLA into sliding-window autoregressive video diffusion pipelines to enable minute-scale rollouts with lower streaming memory and compute overhead.
impact: Provides a practical, architecture-level efficiency improvement for building minute-scale autoregressive video generators—lower memory and latency make long-horizon video synthesis more feasible for researchers and deployed systems.
visual_elements: Before/after schematic: standard per-head KV cache (many parallel KV blocks) vs shared low-rank latent KV cache (single compact dictionary + head projections).
Memory vs rollout length chart comparing per-head KV cache and MLA, highlighting reduced memory growth over minutes.
Pipeline diagram showing sliding-window autoregressive rollout with MLA integrated, indicating where the latent cache is stored and reused.
Qualitative timeline: frames sampled across a minute-long generation to illustrate sustained quality.
paper_title: VideoMLA: Low-Rank Latent KV Cache for Minute-Scale Autoregressive Video Diffusion
paper_authors: Hidir Yesiltepe, Jiazhen Hu, Tuna Han Salih Meral, Adil Kaan Akan, Kaan Oktay
